title: Manifest of a voice pack (manifest.json)
description: Each part (role part, base part, protocol core) has a manifest.json in its directory, listing every file of that part and its SHA-256. The three kinds of manifest are told apart by the part field. This schema covers structure only; rules a schema cannot express (ordering, path safety, duplicate names, references that resolve) are written in FORMAT.md「4. Manifest (manifest.json)」 and checked by protocol/lib/manifest.mjs. Within one major version, minor versions only add and never remove: fields that are not recognized are always ignored on read, so additionalProperties: false is not written here.

madeWith.description: The base part version used to make the pack (the version number that comes after "Made with"). It does not record which pack this pack came from.

requires.description: Requirements on the base part: the protocol major version, and the minimum version of the base part.

features.description: The required capabilities of each feature. The key is the feature name; capabilities in the value are taken from the base part's capability vocabulary (vocab/capabilities.json). When the environment lacks a capability, only the features that use it report an error.

holdout.description: Held-out recording: used only to measure fidelity, never as a reference. It records the language only, with no reference tag and no cue annotation.

externals.description: External resources: not in the pack but placed at a URL and checked by SHA-256. They are referenced by path, treated the same as files inside the pack.

scripts.description: Scripts: register the entry and the runtime, and declare no permissions. The entry must be a file inside the pack.

enhancers.description: Enhancers: files that work only for a given model and give higher fidelity on that model. The pack does not depend on enhancers.

direction.description: The structured part of the dubbing guidance: a one-sentence voice description and voice tags (taken from the design vocabulary).

sampleLines.description: Sample lines: a few lines this voice would say, one line per item. A line may carry a stage cue, for example（耳语） (whisper); the format stores only this string and does not parse it. An item must not be only whitespace or invisible characters (semantic rule, see FORMAT.md「4.5 Semantic rules」).

cardLine.description: Audition line: one line shown on the preview card (text) and its recording (audio, a file inside the pack, an entry in files, dubbed with this pack's own voice), optionally with the seed used to dub it (seed). The line is written like a sample line: it may carry a stage cue, the format stores only this string and does not parse it, and it must not be only whitespace or invisible characters (semantic rule, see FORMAT.md「4.5 Semantic rules」). It is not a reference and not a held-out recording: dubbing, voice conversion, fidelity measurement and picking the default segment never read it.

expressiveness.description: The expressiveness taken for this line alone (an integer from 0 to 100): optional, present only if it was stated explicitly when the pack was made.

seed.description: The seed handed to the synthesis capability when this line was dubbed (an integer from 0 to 2^53−1): present only if the environment accepts a seed. When this line is dubbed again with the same request, the make-pack program changes the seed (adds 1 to the previous one), so it has to be recorded; the format stores only this number, and whoever reads it does not use it for anything else.

expressiveness.description: The expressiveness of this voice (a global value, an integer from 0 to 100): optional. At dubbing time it is used when no later layer declares an expressiveness; the setup's expressiveness (in setups) and the one given at dubbing time override it.

setups.description: Several setups: write the fixed values for how to speak at dubbing time into the pack (emotion, style, energy, language, default reference tag referenceTag, speed, a note for the model), for example one setup named 「平静播报」 (calm announcing) and one named 「生气」 (angry). Each setup has a name, and names must be unique within one pack (semantic rule, see FORMAT.md「4.5 Semantic rules」); at most one setup carries default: true (semantic rule), and dubbing uses it when no setup is named. The values of a setup may be changed in place in the current version (the version number stays the same, only that one directory changes), or a new version may be released; packs already released and copies elsewhere do not change with it; which setup dubbing uses is a parameter of the dubbing (it can also state that this time no setup is used at all, not even the one with default), and is not in the manifest. For how to write the minimum base part version (requires.baseMin) of a pack with setups, see the setups row in FORMAT.md section 4.4.

verification.description: Verification record: in which environment, with which model, on which day it was tested, what the fidelity was, and the evaluation models used to measure that fidelity.

measuredBy.description: The evaluation models used to measure this fidelity: one model name each for speaker verification and blind listening. If you do not know which model it was, leave that item out; if you know neither, leave out measuredBy.

designSource.description: Design source: for a designed voice, records the description, the model used, and the lines used for the audition during design.

auditionLines.description: Design audition text: the original text used for the audition during design, one passage per item. An item must not be only whitespace or invisible characters (semantic rule, see FORMAT.md「4.5 Semantic rules」).

runtimes.description: Registers the command-line tools (names in env.runtimes) that this part's programs need from the runtime environment, for example ffmpeg. It is the same concept and the same spelling as the runtime of a role part script. optional true: if the environment lacks it, only the features that use it report an error and the others work as usual; false: this part cannot work at all without it. purpose says what it is used for.

referenceSet.description: Reference set: several segments of original voice, each with a verbatim transcript, a language and one reference tag. defaultSegment is the default segment of the main language (its language is the pack's main language); languageDefaults are the default segments of the other languages (segment ids, at most one segment per language, optional).

segment.description: One reference segment: an audio file, a verbatim transcript, a cue annotation (optional), a language, a reference tag. tag is used only to switch between the reference segments of one pack (names must be unique within one language, for the semantic rule see FORMAT.md「4.5 Semantic rules」); it is free text, Chinese or English both work.

holdoutSegment.description: One held-out recording: an audio file, a verbatim transcript, a language. It is not used as a reference and needs no switching, so it has no reference tag and no cue annotation.

referenceTag.description: Reference tag: a short name for one reference segment, for example 「愤怒」 (angry), 「少年」 (youth), 「平常」 (normal), 1–64 characters (counted by code point). Compared character by character: names that differ in case are two tags. The referenceTag of a setup uses it to point to a default reference segment.

legacySegment.description: How a reference segment and a held-out recording were written in packs of protocol 1.x and 2.x (only for reading and checking old packs, this version does not write it): language, emotion, style and energy are written in tags. Manifests of protocol 3.x do not use it; they use segment and holdoutSegment (FORMAT.md section 14).

annotatedText.description: Cue annotation: the whole sentence of a reference segment's verbatim transcript with square-bracket cues added where the way of speaking changes, for example [laughs]呵呵，[happy]太可爱了吧。 (the Chinese reads roughly "hehe, so cute!"). Apart from the cues, the characters are the same as text. At dubbing time it is handed to the model together with the reference. If there is none, do not write this key.

languageTag.description: Language tag: 2 to 3 letters, optionally followed by several groups of "hyphen + 2 to 8 letters or digits", for example en, zh-CN, zh-Hans-CN; underscores are not accepted (zh_CN is invalid). It is written the same way as the language of a reference segment, of a held-out recording, and of a setup's labels.language.

energyLevel.description: Energy: three levels, low, medium, high. The labels.energy of a setup uses it (tags.energy of a reference segment of protocol 1.x and 2.x is written the same way).

setup.description: One setup: name is the name; labels are the fixed labels (language, emotion, style, energy, all optional; not the same set as the reference tag of a reference segment); referenceTag is the default reference of this setup, pointing by the reference tag of a reference segment (optional, must be the tag of some segment in the reference set, for the semantic rule see FORMAT.md「4.5 Semantic rules」); speed is the speed multiplier, a positive number (1 is unchanged, 0.85 slows down, 1.15 speeds up), and dubbing changes the speed by it after synthesis (this is not the slow-down or speed-up cue written in a script and handed to the model); expressiveness is the fixed expressiveness of this voice, an integer from 0 to 100, used when the caller gives none at dubbing time (optional); instructions is a note for the model, for example accent or dialect; the setup with default true is the one used when none is named.

fileList.description: Every file in this part's directory except the manifest and the signature, sorted by the UTF-8 byte order of the path. Subdirectories that have a manifest of their own (the base part, the protocol core) are handled by that manifest and are not listed here.

packPath.description: Path relative to this part's directory, separated by /. This catches only the most obvious forms (empty, starting with /, containing a backslash); leaving the directory, an empty segment, and Windows reserved names are checked by manifest.mjs according to FORMAT.md「Path check」.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the raw bytes of the file, lowercase hexadecimal. Line breaks are not converted.

size.description: The size of the file in bytes.

protocolVersion.description: Protocol version, two segments "major.minor". Compatible within one major version; minor versions only add and never remove.

packId.description: Pack ID: "short English name-8 random lowercase letters and digits". It follows the Agent Skills restrictions on name: only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 64 characters, no hyphen at the start or end, no two hyphens in a row.

slug.description: The name given to an entry in the manifest: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores.

capabilityName.description: The name of a required capability, taken from the capability vocabulary.

runtimeName.description: The name of a runtime: a command-line tool provided by the runtime environment, taken from the keys of env.runtimes, for example ffmpeg, node. The runtime of a role part script and runtimes[].runtime registered by the base part both use this one spelling: starts with a lowercase letter, followed by lowercase letters, digits, dots, underscores, plus signs, hyphens, at most 32 characters.
